clue.text: Power-mad criminal

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
mad in the sense of furious, angry

explanation.surface: A power-crazed villain bent on domination.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer who robs ships at sea is a lawbreaker, so a criminal of a specific kind.

clue.text: Bar where spin doctors congregate?

definitions.meaning: to bar is to stop or block
spin doctors work in PR, so a public relations event is where they gather

explanation.surface: A pub where political spin doctors gather.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as PR EVENT, the second reading is a gathering of publicists; 'Bar' looks like a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to stop it happening, the verb sense of hinder.

clue.text: Joint Head of Enterprise leaves for transfer

indicators.note: leaves means the named letter departs from the word

parts.note: a reefer is a cannabis joint

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The joint head of a company departs for a new posting.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer a case or patient is to pass it on to someone else.

clue.text: Material from humorist ultimately old hat

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: ex means former
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Fabric taken from a comedian's dated headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A textile is woven or knitted fabric, a material.

clue.text: Like some drinks, talking with old therapist

indicators.note: talking signals that the drinks word is to be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: sparkling drinks are described as fizzy

explanation.surface: Chatting with an elderly therapist about carbonated drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for physiotherapist, someone who treats injuries with exercise and massage.

clue.text: Chinese race finished in George's house?

parts.note: the Han are China's majority ethnic group
over means finished

explanation.surface: A Chinese race has ended at George's home.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Hanover was the royal dynasty of the four King Georges.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal house is a dynasty; the Georges belonged to the Hanoverian line.

clue.text: Settled down with your picture book from Rome

parts.note: sat means settled into a seat
yr is a written abbreviation for your
an icon is a picture or image

explanation.surface: Sitting down with your illustrated book from Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Satyricon is a Latin novel by Petronius from imperial Rome.

clue.text: Humming note, run round America with nothing on

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed on top

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
do is a note of the sol-fa scale
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is round in shape
US is America

explanation.surface: Humming a tune while jogging around America naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Humming is slang for smelling strongly, so having a pronounced scent.

clue.text: One dope hugs second daughter in Shakespeare

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping round, so these letters enclose another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
gen and dope are both slang for information
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A fool embraces a second daughter from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is Cymbeline's daughter in the Shakespeare play.

clue.text: Doctor Liam Fox in a tense scrutiny of motives

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Liam Fox, the Conservative politician and former GP, anxiously examines why he does things.
explanation.walkthrough: Liam Fox really is a medical doctor, so 'Doctor' reads as his title before it shows itself as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Examining yourself means looking inward at your own reasons and conduct.

clue.text: Monarch's hot, tearing finery with an "eff off"!

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot on taps

indicators.note: tearing apart the fabric of a word reorders its letters
off means the letter named is removed from the fine clothes

parts.note: eff is the spoken name of the letter F

explanation.surface: An angry king rips at his robes and swears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eff off' also reads as a euphemistic curse. FINERY without F leaves INERY, which 'tearing' rearranges to ENRYI.
explanation.definitionFit: The first English king of that name, son of William the Conqueror, reigned 1100-1135.

clue.text: Ex-minister meeting resistance — and not a leader

parts.note: Michael Gove, former UK cabinet minister
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
nor means and not

explanation.surface: A former minister faces opposition and is no longer in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor heads a state, colony or institution, so is someone in charge.

clue.text: Ruling nationalist's way to encourage progress

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
to urge someone on is to spur them forward

explanation.surface: How a governing nationalist pushes things forward.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicola Sturgeon led the Scottish National Party and the Scottish government when this appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's First Minister from the SNP was the nationalist then in power.

clue.text: Governess's favourite eggs are picked up without box

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around the box
picked up means heard, so the eggs phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: fish eggs are roe, so roe are said aloud
a chest is a box

explanation.surface: A governess's favourite eggs are collected from outside a box.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Eyre, governess in Charlotte Brontë's novel, loves Mr Rochester.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Rochester is the man Jane Eyre the governess falls for and marries.

clue.text: Carmen is close to perfect for discriminating fellow

parts.note: read as car men: the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Bizet's Carmen comes near to perfection for a discerning listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carmen' must be split into car men, the RAC (the British motoring breakdown club).
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot who treats people unfairly by ethnicity discriminates against them.

clue.text: Two coppers arresting a small group of politicians

indicators.note: police arresting someone hold them, so these letters enclose another

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, taken twice
S is the abbreviation for small on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A pair of police officers detain a small political faction.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a meeting or bloc of party members who decide policy or candidates.

clue.text: A rubbish country welcomes right modernising leader

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A trashy nation takes in a right-wing reformer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kemal Atatürk founded modern Turkey and westernised its laws and script.

clue.text: Popular turns adopted by a cast working like hell

indicators.note: adopted by means taken into, so the reversed word goes inside
working suggests letters being worked into a new shape
turns means the word is read backwards

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: Pop acts are taken on by a cast working furiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular turns' reads like pop acts, but 'turns' reverses the word for popular; 'working' rearranges A CAST to SATAC, which 'adopted by' wraps around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell is the Devil's domain, so devilish things are like hell.

clue.text: Muslim country in revolt, having to convert to Catholicism

indicators.note: in places the country inside the uprising

parts.note: a rising is a revolt
Oman is a Muslim sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A Muslim nation in revolution being made to adopt Catholicism.
explanation.definitionFit: To Romanise is to bring under the Church of Rome, making something Roman Catholic.

clue.text: Painter captures something magical in land

indicators.note: capturing holds something inside, so these letters enclose another

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
a wand is a magician's tool

explanation.surface: An artist depicts something enchanted in a landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is an African country, a land.

clue.text: Two spies together with a red

parts.note: M is the spy chief in the Bond stories and an agent is a spy

explanation.surface: Two spies team up with a communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' looks like a communist, fitting the spies, but is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red colour, a shade of red.

clue.text: Republican brought in to agitate gets a foothold

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside

parts.note: to stir up is to agitate

explanation.surface: A Republican is drafted in to stir trouble and establishes a base.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup is the loop a rider's foot rests in, literally a hold for the foot.

clue.text: Piano star drunk on beer, where classical training took place

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A piano virtuoso gets drunk on beer.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece and Rome a wrestling school or gymnasium was where athletes trained.

clue.text: Banks maybe withdraw a false statement

parts.note: to go is to leave or withdraw
a lie is a false statement

explanation.surface: Banks might retract a misleading claim.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Banks was England's goalkeeper in the 1966 World Cup; 'Banks' pretends to be financial institutions.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon Banks is a famous example of a goalkeeper, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: What a doctor has, catching current bug

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so these letters enclose another

parts.note: a doctor of philosophy holds a PhD
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A doctor catches an infection that's going around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like an illness the doctor catches; it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenfly is a sap-sucking insect, a garden bug.

clue.text: Seeking academics to engage somewhere near Cambridge

parts.note: hunting means seeking
dons are university teachers
to engage staff is to hire them

explanation.surface: Looking for scholars to recruit near Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Huntingdonshire is a former English county, now part of Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a district neighbouring Cambridge, so an example of a nearby place.

clue.text: Brandy drinks before church

parts.note: kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur, here plural

explanation.surface: Having drinks before going to church.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirsch is a clear cherry brandy from Germany and Switzerland.

clue.text: American wears top out of bed or stuck in it

indicators.note: something worn goes around the wearer, so the cover encloses a letter

parts.note: a lid is a top
up means risen from bed

explanation.surface: An American in a hat, either up and about or confined to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to bed: being stuck in bed means ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confined to bed through illness is said to be laid up.
